The interrogative `הֲ` takes the fronted *Are* under rule 20's closing sentences on an interrogative verbless clause; the explicit pronoun keeps only *they* and the fused `בְּעֵבֶר` keeps only *beyond*.

`דֶּרֶךְ` here holds an English noun of its own (*the way*), so rule 19's preposition-for-lexeme rider does not apply and the *of*s go to the successive recta; the three written *the*s are counted so that the only article morpheme, on `הַשָּׁמֶשׁ`, takes the one before its own word.
`מוּל` → *over against* is headed on *against* as the word carrying the relation; heading on *over* was the competing reading and is named.
